question: A 23-year-old gravida-1-para-1 (G1P1) presents to the emergency department with fever, malaise, nausea, and abdominal pain. She says her symptoms started 2 days ago with a fever and nausea, which have progressively worsened. 2 hours ago, she started having severe lower abdominal pain that is diffusely localized. Her past medical history is unremarkable. Her last menstrual period was 3 weeks ago. She has had 3 sexual partners in the past month and uses oral contraception. The vital signs include temperature 38.8°C (102.0°F) and blood pressure 120/75 mm Hg. On physical examination, the lower abdomen is severely tender to palpation with guarding. Uterine and adnexal tenderness is also elicited. A urine pregnancy test is negative. On speculum examination, the cervix is inflamed with positive cervical motion tenderness and the presence of a scant yellow-white purulent discharge. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "23-year-old female with fever and abdominal pain" -> "symptoms suggest possible infection" -> "negative urine pregnancy test" -> "cervical motion tenderness present" -> "purulent discharge observed" -> "likely pelvic inflammatory disease" -> 85%

CHAIN: "Patient presents with fever and malaise" -> "lower abdominal pain is severe and diffuse" -> "guarding and tenderness on examination" -> "cervical inflammation noted" -> "presence of purulent discharge" -> "consistent with cervicitis or pelvic inflammatory disease" -> "more symptoms align with pelvic inflammatory disease" -> 90%

CHAIN: "Fever and nausea for 2 days" -> "progression to severe abdominal pain" -> "negative pregnancy test reduces ectopic pregnancy likelihood" -> "cervical motion tenderness indicates possible infection" -> "purulent discharge suggests cervicitis" -> "but also supports pelvic inflammatory disease" -> "most likely diagnosis is pelvic inflammatory disease" -> 88%

CHAIN: "Patient has multiple sexual partners" -> "risk factor for sexually transmitted infections" -> "cervical inflammation and purulent discharge present" -> "symptoms align with cervicitis" -> "but also suggest pelvic inflammatory disease" -> "considering the severity of symptoms" -> "pelvic inflammatory disease is most likely" -> 87%
analysis: The patient's symptoms of fever, malaise, nausea, and severe lower abdominal pain, along with the presence of cervical motion tenderness and purulent discharge, suggest an infection of the reproductive organs. The negative urine pregnancy test rules out ectopic pregnancy, and the combination of symptoms aligns with pelvic inflammatory disease (PID), which is characterized by inflammation of the uterus, fallopian tubes, and surrounding structures, often due to sexually transmitted infections. Therefore, the most likely diagnosis is pelvic inflammatory disease.
